newsitem.title: CHILE: Toy soldier of Pinochet irks Chilean army.
newsitem.headline: Toy soldier of Pinochet irks Chilean army.

text.p: The Chilean army has asked a sculptor to stop making toy soldiers of former military ruler Gen. Augusto Pinochet, the artist said on Thursday.
"They've asked me to please stop making, selling and distributing them until the general can review them," sculptor Juan Antonio Santis said.

Pinochet's admirers have been buying up the three-inch (7 cm) lead figures of the former strongman by the dozen. Santis said the army called to ask him to hold off until Pinochet approves the toy figures of the smiling general wearing full uniform and a flowing military cape.
The hand-painted figures sell for $29 at a hobby shop that specialises in military models and toy soldiers.
"We've been sold out of the Pinochet figurine for several days now. We've got a waiting list of people ready to buy them," said the shop owner's daughter, Janina Aragon.
Santis said his work was not a homage to Pinochet, who ruled Chile with an iron fist from 1973 to 1990 and is still a very controversial figure as commander-in-chief of the army.
"This is not a tribute to Pinochet but rather a recreation of a person who is historic whether you like him or not."
